arguments.claim: Frontal X-ray of the pelvis shows bilateral hip abnormalities. The right femoral head epiphysis is displaced inferiorly and posteriorly relative to the femoral neck. The physis is widened. The neck-shaft angle is decreased (coxa vara). The left hip also shows epiphyseal displacement.
Post-operative X-rays show screw fixation in both hips. The right hip has multiple screws, and the left hip has a single large cannulated screw. This is consistent with in-situ pinning for SCFE.
Annotated image shows neck-shaft angles: Right hip 81 degrees (coxa vara), Left hip 146 degrees. This confirms the deformity associated with the slip.

hypotheses.name: Bilateral Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis (SCFE), post-operative
hypotheses.rationale: Classic presentation in an obese 12-year-old with hip pain and limp. X-rays show bilateral epiphyseal displacement with widened physes. Post-operative screw fixation is present in both hips, consistent with in-situ pinning. The right hip shows more severe deformity (coxa vara) and multiple screws.

hypotheses.name: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease
hypotheses.rationale: Can cause hip pain and limp in children, but typically affects younger children (4-8 years). The radiographic appearance is of a slip rather than fragmentation and sclerosis typical of Perthes.

hypotheses.name: Septic Arthritis
hypotheses.rationale: Acute pain and inability to bear weight could suggest this, but the chronic history and specific radiographic findings of epiphyseal slip make SCFE much more likely.

arguments.note: Updated hypotheses based on X-ray findings showing bilateral SCFE with post-operative fixation.

differential_diagnoses.name: Septic Arthritis
differential_diagnoses.why: Could present with acute hip pain and inability to bear weight, but the chronic history (weeks of pain and limp) and specific radiographic findings of epiphyseal slip with widened physis make SCFE much more likely. No joint space narrowing or periarticular osteopenia suggestive of infection.
